name: Sitagliptin and metformin
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero
summary: This fixed combination pairs sitagliptin 50 mg with metformin 500 mg, 850 mg or 1 g. The US label contraindicates it below an estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) of 30 mL/min/1.73 m2 (metformin, lactic acidosis) and does not recommend it at eGFR 30 to 44, because sitagliptin then needs a lower dose than the tablet provides. Below eGFR 45, use the components separately; below 30, metformin is contraindicated.

bands.recommendation: Usual: one tablet twice daily with meals; maximum sitagliptin 100 mg and metformin 2,000 mg per day. Check eGFR before starting and periodically (label).

eGFR 45–59: usual dose. eGFR 30–44: not recommended (sitagliptin needs 50 mg/day, which the tablet cannot give); use the components separately: sitagliptin 50 mg daily plus metformin (do not start metformin at eGFR 30–45; if continuing, guidelines cap it at 1,000 mg/day).
Contraindicated below eGFR 30 (metformin; label). Use the components separately: sitagliptin alone at 25 mg once daily (sitagliptin label).
Contraindicated (eGFR <30; label). Use the components separately: sitagliptin alone at 25 mg once daily.

hd: Contraindicated (metformin; eGFR <30). Use the components separately: sitagliptin alone at 25 mg once daily, any time relative to dialysis (sitagliptin label).
pd: Contraindicated (metformin; eGFR <30). Use the components separately: sitagliptin alone at 25 mg once daily.
crrt: Not appropriate: metformin contraindicated in severe kidney impairment and acute kidney injury raises lactic acidosis risk (label).
dialyzable: Metformin: yes, clearance up to 170 mL/min under good hemodynamic conditions. Sitagliptin: modestly, about 13.5% removed in a 3- to 4-hour session; peritoneal dialysis removal unknown (label 10).
monitoring: eGFR before starting and at least yearly; more often if eGFR <60 or at risk. Stop at or before iodinated contrast if eGFR 30–60, liver disease, alcoholism, heart failure or intra-arterial contrast; recheck eGFR at 48 hours (label 2.3). Hold during acute illness, dehydration or surgery. Vitamin B12 with long-term use. Hypoglycemia with insulin or sulfonylureas.

adult: Component doses in red and amber tiles come from the approved sitagliptin and metformin records (sitagliptin 50 mg at eGFR 30–44 and 25 mg below 30; metformin 1,000 mg/day cap at 30–44 from KDIGO 2022 and ADA-KDIGO 2022).
PH strengths 50/500, 50/850 and 50/1000 mg match US (the selected label lists 50/500 and 50/1000 mg tablets; 50/850 mg is a PH strength).
PD sitagliptin 25 mg is from the sitagliptin label (approved record).
